headline: Geopolitical Storm Clouds Gather Over Monday's Open
body_html:
Wall Street heads into Monday's session on a cautious footing as escalating Middle East tensions dominate the overnight narrative. Houthi strikes on Riyadh's airport drew condemnation from Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia over the weekend, while the FAA issued a safety advisory urging U.S. carriers to exercise caution on Saudi routes. Top oil executives withdrew from a scheduled Riyadh event, and Iran's rejection of U.S. overtures on the Strait of Hormuz kept energy markets on edge heading into the open.

Friday's completed session offered a more constructive backdrop. Of the 544 names in our universe, 344 advanced against 196 decliners. Healthcare led all sectors, gaining 1.45%, while Software added 1.04%. Telehealth name Hims & Hers Health surged 10.19% to top the leaderboard, followed by security-software firm Zscaler at 7.80% and data-cloud platform Snowflake at 7.42%. On the downside, Homebuilders dropped 1.44% and Semiconductors slipped 0.48%, with audio-chip maker Cirrus Logic and RF specialist Skyworks Solutions each shedding more than 5%.

Beyond the Middle East, traders will be tracking the dollar, which held near an 18-month high Friday as U.S. inflation data remained squarely in focus. A surprise Ukraine energy ceasefire announced by President Trump added another variable to an already complex macro picture. Expect volatility at the open as markets digest weekend headlines before Tuesday's session brings fresh catalysts.

briefs.headline: FAA Flags Saudi Airspace Risk as Houthi Strikes Hit Riyadh Airport
briefs.body: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration instructed American airlines to exercise caution on Saudi Arabian routes following Houthi missile and drone strikes on Riyadh's main airport. One Indian national wounded in the attack has since died, according to the country's embassy. Energy and airline-adjacent names could see early pressure at Monday's open.

briefs.headline: Iran Rejects U.S. Hormuz Proposal, Keeping Strait Risk Elevated
briefs.body: Tehran declared that Washington's response to its proposal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz was inadequate, leaving a key global oil chokepoint in diplomatic limbo. Analysts note that the oil market's center of gravity has been drifting eastward, amplifying the strategic weight of any Hormuz disruption. Crude-linked equities warrant close attention at the bell.

briefs.headline: Trump Announces Ukraine Energy Ceasefire, Zelenskiy Caught Off Guard
briefs.body: President Trump revealed a ceasefire agreement with Russia limited to Ukrainian energy infrastructure, a move that appeared to surprise Kyiv. The announcement adds an unexpected geopolitical variable for European energy markets and could ripple into U.S. liquefied-natural-gas export names. Markets will be parsing the fine print through Monday's session.

briefs.headline: Dollar Holds Near 18-Month Peak Ahead of Inflation Data
briefs.body: The greenback steadied close to its strongest level in a year and a half as investors weighed Middle East conflict risk alongside upcoming U.S. inflation figures. A firm dollar historically creates headwinds for multinational earnings and commodity prices. Currency-sensitive sectors including Materials, which eked out only a 0.37% gain Friday, may face continued scrutiny.

briefs.headline: Healthcare and Software Lead Friday's Advance, Semis Lag
briefs.body: Friday's session saw clear sector divergence, with Healthcare rising 1.45% and Software adding 1.04% to pace the field. Semiconductors slid 0.48%, dragged by Cirrus Logic's 5.59% drop and Skyworks Solutions' 5.45% decline. Homebuilders fared worst of all tracked sectors, falling 1.44% as rate-sensitive housing names remained under pressure.

briefs.headline: Saudi-Iran Diplomatic Contact Offers Thin Reed of De-Escalation Hope
briefs.body: The Saudi and Iranian foreign ministers held discussions over regional tensions, according to state media, offering a faint signal that back-channel diplomacy remains active despite the weekend's violence. Analysts caution that any progress is fragile given simultaneous strikes on Yemen's Sanaa airport and Iran's hard line on Hormuz. The exchange may limit the most extreme risk-off moves at Monday's open.
